sources.title: MSVO 3, 79 artifact entry (P005390)
sources.author: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative; transliterations by Robert K. Englund, Jacob L. Dahl and CDLI
sources.type: primary artifact record and corpus transliteration
sources.authority: CDLI object-level record linked to the Metropolitan Museum of Art
locators: Text: obverse columns 1–2 and reverse columns 1–2
Edition references: MSVO 3 no. 79; Frühe Schrift no. 4.79; CTMMA IV no. 180
sources.limitations: CDLI labels Uruk provenience uncertain and dates the tablet to Uruk III ca. 3200–3000 BCE; the Met uses Jemdet Nasr ca. 3100–2900 BCE. Language is undetermined and the document lacks verbs, limiting transaction-level interpretation.
sources.notes: Selected administrative object. Contemporary ancient tablet, not a later copy; use as an early economic-classification case, not a transparent voice.

sources.title: Cuneiform tablet: administrative account concerning the distribution of barley and emmer
sources.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.limitations: The museum gives 'probably from Uruk' and a broad interpretive description; acquisition rather than excavation context means exact provenience is uncertain.
sources.notes: Rights anchor for the selected administrative object: Met object images are marked Public Domain; credit the museum and object number.

sources.title: Cuneiform tablet: private letter
sources.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.type: primary artifact record with scholarly overview
locators: Overview: Marduk-mushallim's report on non-implementation of a royal security order
Artwork details: Old Babylonian, ca. 1632 BCE, probably Sippar-Yahrurum
sources.limitations: Purchased in 1886; exact archaeological context is unavailable and geography is qualified as probable. The letter is unusual, so it cannot represent ordinary correspondence.
sources.notes: Selected epistolary object. Treat as an ancient documentary letter, not an Old Babylonian school copy. Met object images are marked Public Domain; modern translation wording is not cleared for direct quotation.

sources.title: N 6052 (+) UM 29-16-393 artifact entry (P228744)
sources.author: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative / Digital Corpus of Cuneiform Lexical Texts
sources.type: primary artifact record, transliteration and composite witness
locators: CDLI P228744; museum nos. N 6052 (+) UM 29-16-393
Witness to CDLI Lexical 000001 / composite Q000001
sources.limitations: Fragmented Old Babylonian school tablet; obverse is not preserved and findspot/stratigraphic fields are blank. It represents formal lexical training at Nippur, not general literacy.
sources.notes: Selected knowledge/training object. Excavated at Nippur, ca. 1900–1600 BCE. CDLI provides transliteration; the photograph is marked © Penn Museum and requires a separate image-use check.

sources.title: Letter from Puzur-Shulgi to Ibbi-Suen about Ishbi-Erra's claim on Isin (ETCSL 3.1.19)
sources.author: Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature, University of Oxford
sources.authority: Curated Sumerian literary corpus with manuscript list and edition bibliography
locators: Cuneiform witnesses include 3N-T311 = IM 58418 and IM 13347; full witness list in bibliography
sources.limitations: The online text is a modern composite reconstructed from multiple Old Babylonian school manuscripts. It is not a surviving contemporary Ur III letter or a single speaker's unmediated voice.
sources.notes: Selected literary-memory text. The narrated setting belongs to the end of Ur III, while the surviving manuscripts are later Old Babylonian copies.
